query: What features can be extracted to train a model to predict a review's score?

per_column.name: text_length
per_column.rationale: Character count of the review text is known before the outcome and is a weak but legitimate predictor; verbose reviews often correlate with more critical or extreme scores.

per_column.name: word_count
per_column.rationale: Token count of the text is a valid external feature; carries modest signal (length correlates with sentiment polarity), though largely redundant with text_length.

per_column.name: helpfulness_ratio
per_column.rationale: Derived from HelpfulnessNumerator/Denominator, which are separate from the score. Helpfulness is community feedback that plausibly correlates with score and does not deterministically encode it; a legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: summary_length
per_column.rationale: Length of the summary field is external to the score and plausibly carries weak signal similar to text length.

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Exclamation frequency is a genuine stylistic/affective feature outside the focus and plausibly correlates with enthusiasm and thus higher scores.

per_column.name: question_count
per_column.rationale: Count of question marks is an external stylistic feature that can signal confusion or dissatisfaction; weak but legitimate signal.

per_column.name: uppercase_ratio
per_column.rationale: Proportion of uppercase characters proxies emphasis/shouting, an affective signal outside the score; plausible weak predictor.

per_column.name: positive_keyword_count
per_column.rationale: Lexicon-based positive term count is a sentiment feature derived from text, not from the score, and is a strong plausible predictor of higher scores.

per_column.name: negative_keyword_count
per_column.rationale: Negative term count is a sentiment feature external to the focus and a strong plausible predictor of lower scores.

per_column.name: review_year
per_column.rationale: Year derived from Time is external to the score and can capture temporal drift in rating behavior; a legitimate weak predictor.

judge.rationale: All ten added columns are legitimate predictors: each is derived from text, metadata, or helpfulness signals that lie outside review_score and involve no leakage. The set is dominated by generic surface-text statistics (length, word count, summary length, punctuation, uppercase ratio) which carry only weak, partly redundant signal. The genuinely useful features are the sentiment-lexicon counts (positive/negative keyword counts), plus helpfulness_ratio and review_year. Because the strongest predictive leverage rests on a couple of crude lexicon counts while the rest is mechanical, the set provides moderate but not strong incremental predictive power beyond the original columns.
